content.text: I have a clear picture of the issue. Let me now resolve the ticket.

input.note:
**Root Cause: CPU request exceeds the capacity of every node in the cluster.**

**Evidence observed:**
- Pod `trainer-q3-full-5d8f7c4b9-jw2rx` is stuck in `Pending` with scheduler message: *"0/6 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 6 No preemption victims found for incoming pod."*
- The updated Q3 trainer config sets a CPU request/limit of **16 cores**.
- Your node pool is **m6i.2xlarge (8 vCPU)**. Even an entirely empty node cannot satisfy a 16-core request — no amount of waiting or freeing other pods will fix this; the pod can **never** be scheduled on the current nodes.
- By comparison, last week's Q2 trainer (`trainer-q2-full-7b4c9d6f8-pl4mz`) requested only **6 CPU**, which fits comfortably on an 8-vCPU node and completed successfully.

**Why this happens:**
The Kubernetes scheduler places a pod on a node only when the node's allocatable CPU is greater than or equal to the pod's CPU request. Because system daemons also consume a portion of each node's capacity, the effective allocatable CPU on an 8-vCPU node is slightly less than 8 cores [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#how-pods-with-resource-requests-are-scheduled-0]. A request of 16 cores exceeds any single node's total capacity, so scheduling is impossible [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/assign-cpu-resource#specify-a-cpu-request-that-is-too-big-for-your-nodes-0][cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-1].

**Fix — choose one of the following:**

1. **(Recommended if 16 cores aren't actually needed)** Reduce the CPU `request` and `limit` in the trainer Job/Pod spec to a value that fits within the allocatable capacity of an m6i.2xlarge node (≤ ~7.5 cores to leave room for system daemons). The Q2 run used 6 cores successfully — revisit whether the Q3 dataset truly requires doubling that.

2. **(If 16 cores are genuinely required)** Add a node pool of larger instances (e.g., m6i.4xlarge = 16 vCPU or m6i.8xlarge = 32 vCPU) and either update the trainer pod spec to tolerate/select those nodes, or ensure the scheduler can place the pod there [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-1].

After making either change, delete the stuck pod (it will be recreated by its controller) and confirm it transitions to `Running`.
